label: Red fox (Canidae, canine representative)

image.species_shown: Vulpes vulpes (red fox) chosen as representative; no image was obtained

physical_parsing.volume_method: Whole-body volume estimated as adult mass (about 5.5 kg, midpoint of the 3-7 kg range) divided by body density of about 1000 kg/m3. The fur-inflated bounding box is not used because it grossly overestimates volume for a slender canid. Legs and tail are folded into this estimate, not added separately.
physical_parsing.shape_class: Quadruped: horizontal ellipsoidal torso with a wedge-shaped tapering head and a long bushy tail; four slender digitigrade legs carry the body roughly 0.3 m above ground.

core.description: Torso as a segmented ellipsoid chain: thorax (forward, under the shoulders), lumbar/abdomen (middle), and pelvis (rear, carrying the hip girdle and tail root). The neck and head attach at the anterior end, and the tail attaches to the dorsal rump.
core.cross_section: Roughly elliptical, about 0.14 m wide by 0.12 m deep at mid-torso, slightly narrower at the waist.

physical_parsing.size_source: Wilson and Mittermeier (2009), Handbook of the Mammals of the World vol. 1 (Carnivores), Vulpes vulpes account, cited from memory: head-body length about 0.6-0.9 m, tail about 0.3-0.5 m, shoulder height about 0.35-0.4 m, adult mass about 3-7 kg. These values were not re-checked online in this session.

parts.name: Foreleg (left)

penetration.overlap_region: Lateral thoracic wall and scapular muscle sling, dorsolateral to the thorax

parts.notes: Digitigrade: the walking surface is the paw, and the carpus is raised. Joint ranges are approximate. The forelimb has no rigid clavicle, so the shoulder is a muscular ball-like attachment.

parts.name: Hindleg (left)

penetration.overlap_region: Dorsolateral pelvis at the hip socket, the acetabulum region of the pelvic girdle

parts.notes: Digitigrade hindleg. The hock is a raised tarsal joint, so the stance is on the toes. The hindleg is slightly longer and thicker than the foreleg (thigh musculature).

parts.name: Forepaw (left)

penetration.overlap_region: None. The paw is a distal segment attached to the carpus of the foreleg and does not touch the core.

parts.notes: Five digits including the dewclaw, with a fleshy metacarpal and digital pads. Ground contact is through the pads.

parts.name: Hindpaw (left)

penetration.overlap_region: None. The paw is a distal segment attached to the hock of the hindleg and does not touch the core.

parts.notes: Four digits with a smaller plantar pad than the forepaw. Ground contact is through the pads.

parts.name: Claws (non-retractable)

penetration.overlap_region: None. Claws are keratin sheaths on the distal phalanges and do not touch the core.

parts.notes: Count is 9 per side: 5 forefoot (four digits plus dewclaw) and 4 hindfoot. Claws are blunt and non-retractable, and they aid traction on the ground.

parts.name: Bushy tail (brush)

penetration.overlap_region: Posterior dorsal rump, the sacrum and caudal vertebrae at the back of the pelvis

parts.notes: Functional roles: balance while running and turning, body heat and insulation, and signalling. The tail is bushy along its length and tapers to a tip, which is often white in red fox.

parts.name: Head and muzzle (wedge-shaped skull)

penetration.overlap_region: Anterior thorax and cervical junction at the front of the torso

parts.notes: Long, narrow, wedge-shaped muzzle, with the skull as a feeding and sensory housing. The head is treated as a feeding structure because the jaws and canines are carried on it. The head is not a separate category in the taxonomy.

parts.name: Jaws with canine teeth

penetration.overlap_region: Cranial base at the zygomatic arch and temporal fossa of the skull

parts.notes: Upper and lower jaws with pointed canines about 0.02-0.025 m exposed. The jaw is a hinge with a mainly vertical gape. The lower jaw is about 0.1 m long. Dentition is carnassial-type, adapted for prey capture and omnivorous feeding.

parts.name: Nose (rhinarium)

penetration.overlap_region: Rostral tip of the muzzle over the nasal bones

parts.notes: Moist rhinarium, important for olfaction. Olfaction is the principal sense for hunting small prey.

parts.name: Eye (left)

penetration.overlap_region: Orbit (eye socket) of the frontal and maxillary bones

parts.notes: Forward-facing eyes with a vertically elliptical pupil, amber iris. Binocular forward vision gives depth perception for hunting.

parts.name: Ear (left, erect)

penetration.overlap_region: Temporal and parietal region of the cranium, rear top of the skull

parts.notes: Large triangular upright ears used for directional hearing of prey under vegetation and snow. Ears rotate on auricular muscles.

parts.name: Vibrissae (whiskers, left)

penetration.overlap_region: Muzzle skin and follicle pad over the maxilla, beside the nose

parts.notes: Tactile whisker pads on the muzzle. Several vibrissae per side, modelled here as a single representative whisker. The library has no matching part.

constraints.symmetry: Bilateral about the sagittal plane (x = 0). Midline parts: tail, head_muzzle, jaws, nose.
constraints.gait: Digitigrade quadruped; diagonal-couplet trot as the typical gait, gallop in fast pursuit. The hock is raised, so the foot strikes on the paw pads and claws.
other: Normalized coordinates use width_x 0.25 m, height_y 0.48 m, length_z 1.1 m. Ground is y = 0, nose at z = +0.5, tail tip at z = -0.5.
Penetration into the core is given for each attached part. Paws and claws are distal, so their penetration depth into the core is 0 (they attach to the limb, not the torso).
Pair counts are per side (1 for L). Claws are 9 per side.
Joint positions are approximate, derived from a standing adult's proportions, not from a skeletal model.

library_gaps.feature: Digitigrade leg segments (shoulder, elbow, carpus; hip, stifle, hock)
library_gaps.why: No library leg part exists. The library has foot parts only, not multi-joint limbs.

library_gaps.feature: Non-retractable claws as a standalone digit structure
library_gaps.why: foot_claw is the nearest hint but is a foot part, not a free-standing claw set with per-digit placement.

library_gaps.feature: Bushy brush tail with a taper and terminal tip
library_gaps.why: tail_tuft and tail_fan are close, but neither models a bushy taper with a tail-length-to-body ratio around 0.4 m.
No library part for multiple fine tactile whiskers on the muzzle.

library_gaps.feature: Digitigrade paw pads and digit set
library_gaps.why: foot_pad is a single pad. It does not model metacarpal and digital pads with a dewclaw.
